deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three blocks of linear elasticity (small displacements u,v,w). It is the kind of material Riemann would need for elastic or rigid-body parts of an ellipsoid/fluid-mechanics study, or for lecture notes.

(A) Displacements with vanishing strain = infinitesimal rigid motions.
- The six conditions are written: 1) u_x=0, 2) v_y=0, 3) w_z=0, 4) v_z+w_y=0, 5) w_x+u_z=0, 6) v_x+u_y=0.
- Second derivatives of u (implicit steps mine):
  - Differentiate 5) in z and use w_z=0: u_zz=0.
  - Differentiate 6) in y and use v_y=0: u_yy=0.
  - Take ∂_z(6)+∂_y(5)−∂_x(4): 2u_yz=0. The written line '2∂²u/∂x∂y=0' should be the mixed y,z derivative; ∂²u/∂x∂y=0 is trivial from 1).
- Together with u_x=0, u is linear in y,z, and likewise for v and w. Riemann concludes:
  - u=a0+cy−bz
  - v=b0+az−cx
  - w=c0+bx−ay
- This is a translation plus an infinitesimal rotation (rotation vector (−a,−b,−c)).

(B) Strain components and their transformation under a rotation of axes about z.
- Notation (Kirchhoff/Clebsch style, engineering shears):
  - x_x=u_x, y_y=v_y, z_z=w_z
  - y_z=v_z+w_y, z_x=w_x+u_z, x_y=u_y+v_x
- New axes: x'=cosφ x+sinφ y, y'=−sinφ x+cosφ y, with the displacement rotated the same way: u'=cosφ u+sinφ v, v'=−sinφ u+cosφ v.
- Chain rule: ∂/∂x=cosφ ∂/∂x'−sinφ ∂/∂y' and ∂/∂y=sinφ ∂/∂x'+cosφ ∂/∂y'.
  - Applied to w and u: w_x=cosφ w_x'−sinφ w_y' and u_z=cosφ u'_z−sinφ v'_z (from u=cosφ u'−sinφ v').
- Substituting u=cosφ u'−sinφ v' and v=sinφ u'+cosφ v' gives:
  - u_x = cos²φ u'_x' + sin²φ v'_y' − cosφ sinφ (v'_x'+u'_y')
  - v_y = sin²φ u'_x' + cos²φ v'_y' + cosφ sinφ (v'_x'+u'_y')
  - v_x+u_y = 2cosφ sinφ (u'_x'−v'_y') + (cos²φ−sin²φ)(v'_x'+u'_y')
- This is the standard transformation law of plane strain (Mohr-circle formulas, shear written as engineering strain).

(C) Torsion of a circular cylinder (axis z).
- Trial displacement: u=−ωyz, v=ωxz, w=0, i.e. each cross-section turns rigidly by angle ωz.
- Strains: x_x=y_y=z_z=0, x_y=−ωz+ωz=0, y_z=ωx, x_z=−ωy.
- With shear modulus λ, the stresses are Y_z=λωx, X_z=−λωy, Z_z=0.
- Traction-free lateral surface: normal (α,β,γ)=(cosφ,sinφ,0); the z-component of the traction is αX_z+βY_z+γZ_z=−λαωy+λβωx.
  - On the circle x=r cosφ, y=r sinφ this vanishes identically, so the boundary condition holds.
- Torque on a cross-section: M=∬(xY_z−yX_z)dxdy=λω∬(x²+y²)dxdy, which is λωπR⁴/2 for radius R (evaluation mine; Riemann only writes the integral).
- The lines T1=λωx, T2=−λωy, T3=0 appear to list the shear stresses with labels in a different order (cf. X_z=−λωy, Y_z=λωx).

The mirrored words in the middle ('L. Riemann', a title-like line) are show-through of ink from the other side of the leaf, not part of the derivation.
errors: Line '2∂²u/∂x∂y=0' (as transcribed) should be 2∂²u/∂y∂z=0, obtained from ∂_z(6)+∂_y(5)−∂_x(4); possibly a misreading rather than Riemann's slip.
T1=λωx, T2=−λωy is inconsistent with X_z=−λωy, Y_z=λωx written just below, if T1,T2 denote the x,y components of the traction on z=const. Likely a labelling slip or different convention.
Torque integral is set up but not evaluated (no error).

results.what: Vanishing of all six strain components implies an infinitesimal rigid motion u=a0+cy−bz, v=b0+az−cx, w=c0+bx−ay
results.modern_name: Kernel of the linear strain operator / infinitesimal rigid displacements (Killing vectors of Euclidean space)
results.usually_credited_to: Cauchy and Navier (1820s); standard in Lamé, Kirchhoff, Clebsch

results.what: Transformation of plane strain components under rotation of axes by angle φ
Torsion of a circular cylinder: u=−ωyz, v=ωxz, w=0 satisfies the traction-free lateral boundary condition; torque = λω∬(x²+y²)dxdy
results.modern_name: Coulomb torsion of a circular shaft (special case of Saint-Venant torsion without warping)
results.usually_credited_to: Coulomb (1784); Navier, Cauchy; general theory Saint-Venant (1855)

deep.surprise_reason: All three computations are textbook linear elasticity of the 1820s–1850s: rigid-motion kernel, strain transformation and circular torsion. They are carried out correctly and in Kirchhoff/Clebsch-style notation. Nothing non-standard appears; at most it documents that Riemann worked through elasticity basics.

checkable.asserts: The rigid-motion displacement has zero strain
